name: SocialComponentServerFacet_RequestStreamerModeDataSync
summary: The client asks for the streamer-mode data sync. A 46-byte record with an 18-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, then TWO raw bytes. Its reader is explicit and unusually direct - FUN_1414dbca0() for the head, then ONE stream write of LENGTH 2 from object +0x20 - so the two bytes are a single fixed 2-byte run and not two separate flags. That distinction matters: two bools and one 2-byte run produce the same bytes here, and only the codec separates them.
purpose: Request that the server synchronise streamer-mode state to this client. The captured pair is 00 00, and both bytes are zero in the only sample, so what the two bytes mean stays unnamed; the field is carried as one bytes(2) run because that is what the reader writes.

created_when: the social component asks for a streamer-mode data sync
lifecycle.if_absent: the client's streamer-mode state is never synchronised. The capture sends it at seq 0x5e, immediately before the title request at 0x5f

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 ae 40, i.e. type index 4142 = 0x102e. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so an 18-byte body makes a 46-byte record.

The reader writes exactly two raw bytes in ONE stream call with the length as a literal argument, so they are one 2-byte run; splitting them into two bools would be an invention the codec does not support. Both bytes are zero in the only capture, so no reading of either is attempted.
